grade.first_issue: The claimed uniform bound on the sizes of members of \(\mathcal G_n\) is false. For the admissible start \(a_1=35\), one gets \(a_2=40\) and \(a_3=42\), so \(m=2\) but \(\mathcal G_3=\{\{5,7\},\{2,5\},\{2,3,7\}\}\) contains a 3-element set. In particular, the assertion that every member of \(\mathcal G_n\) is a minimal hitting set of \(\mathcal G_{n-1}\) is false (for example, \(\{5,7\}\) is not minimal because \(\{5\}\) already hits \(\mathcal G_2\)). This is a false load-bearing assertion under Rule C, and because it removes the central stabilization argument, Rule E's ceiling of 3 applies.
grade.summary: The hitting-set formulation and the deduction of periodicity conditional on stabilization are useful progress, but stabilization is not proved. Besides the false size bound, the quoted claim that bounded-rank intersecting families have only finitely many isomorphism classes is false: stars with arbitrarily many two-element edges give infinitely many such classes. Even finitely many abstract structures would not, together with a bounded decreasing sequence of densities, force stabilization of the labeled families. The final extension from eventual to pure periodicity also uses an invalid alignment inference. Establishing stabilization requires a genuinely new finiteness argument, so the submitted proof does not support the conclusion.
strengths: Correctly reformulates the gcd conditions using hitting sets.
Correctly observes that, if \(\mathcal G_n\) stabilizes, the resulting admissible set is periodic modulo the product of the relevant primes.
Obtains eventual index periodicity correctly, conditional on the unproved stabilization.

errors.description: The bounded-size claim for members of \(\mathcal G_n\) rests on the false assertion that those members are minimal hitting sets; the explicit sequence beginning with 35 already contradicts the resulting bound.

The stated extremal-set-theory result is false: intersecting families of sets of size at most 2 include stars of arbitrarily many edges, yielding infinitely many isomorphism classes. Thus the central stabilization conclusion has no valid proof.

A strictly decreasing sequence of densities can remain bounded below, and finiteness of abstract isomorphism types would not prevent infinitely many changes of the prime labels. Hence the density paragraph does not repair stabilization.

Eventual enumeration of \(C\) does not imply \(a_n=c_{j+n-1}\) with the index determined by \(a_1\); a transient deviation merely gives a different eventual offset, so the stated contradiction is invalid.
